facts.text: Delegated Files.Read.All permission allows ChatGPT to read files accessible to the signed-in user, constrained by both the application's granted scopes and the user's own authorization.

Administrator consent to delegated permissions does not grant ChatGPT an administrator role or application-only access; administrator participation alone does not imply elevated privileges beyond the consented scopes.

Microsoft Entra consent and ChatGPT action enablement are separate steps; consent does not automatically connect individual accounts or enable actions, and existing Microsoft access restrictions still apply.

Microsoft recommends restricting user consent to selected permissions and verified publishers, reviewing all permission requests centrally, and verifying the publisher and application identity before tenant-wide consent.

Review delegated versus application permissions explicitly rather than assuming all consent requests have the same impact; delegated permissions act on behalf of a signed-in user and are limited by that user's access.

recommendations: Review the exact delegated permissions requested and verify they align with the business need before granting consent.
Implement an administrator approval workflow for permission requests to ensure centralized review and control.
Restrict user consent to verified publishers and selected permissions to reduce risk of excessive access.
Verify the identity of the ChatGPT application and publisher before granting tenant-wide consent.
Monitor granted permissions and review existing app permissions regularly to detect any excessive or unnecessary access.
unknowns: Whether the requested delegated permissions Files.Read.All and Sites.Read.All have been reviewed and authorized by an administrator is unknown.
The exact process and controls implemented by the service desk for managing these permissions are unknown.
Whether the Business plan supports specific monitoring or restriction capabilities for these permissions is unknown.
risks: Granting delegated Files.Read.All and Sites.Read.All permissions allows ChatGPT to read all files and sites accessible to the signed-in user, which may include confidential or personal data, posing a data exposure risk if misused.
If administrator consent is granted without proper review, excessive permissions could be authorized, increasing the attack surface or data leakage risk.
Lack of centralized review or monitoring could allow unauthorized or excessive permissions to persist unnoticed.

evidence.text: Microsoft Entra consent and ChatGPT action enablement are separate steps, potentially performed by different administrators. Consent does not automatically connect individual accounts or enable actions. Existing Microsoft access restrictions still apply. Sites.Selected is not supported for live SharePoint search; supported ChatGPT site-collection restrictions are a separate mechanism.

evidence.text: Microsoft permission grants, enabled ChatGPT actions and an individual's account connection are distinct prerequisites. A change to the Microsoft grant can require reviewing or refreshing the connection.

evidence.text:
Microsoft recommends restricting user consent to selected permissions and verified publishers, with other requests reviewed centrally. An administrator approval workflow can support this process. Review existing apps and granted permissions; additional monitoring capabilities depend on licensing.

Before tenant-wide consent, verify the publisher and application identity, understand every requested permission, and match the request to the expected business functionality. Familiarity or widespread use is not sufficient justification. Do not grant permissions that are unexplained or appear excessive; obtain clarification from the publisher.

evidence.text: Where appropriate, consider user assignment restrictions for approved applications. Review delegated versus application permissions explicitly rather than assuming all consent requests have the same impact.

evidence.text:
Delegated access acts for an authenticated user. Both the application's granted scopes and the user's own authorization constrain access. Delegated Files.Read.All permits reading files accessible to that user.

Application permissions operate as the application without a signed-in user. The same permission name can have different implications: application Files.Read.All allows reading tenant files through Microsoft Graph. Application permissions and some privileged delegated scopes need administrator consent.

evidence.text: Consent authorizes specified permissions. An administrator can approve delegated permissions too, so the administrator's participation alone does not establish that the app has application-only access or an administrator role. Inspect the permission type and requested operations.

grounding_reason: All factual claims about delegated permissions, administrator consent implications, and the separation of consent and action enablement are directly supported by the cited evidence (MS-PERM-1, MS-PERM-2, OAI-LIVE-2). The recommended risks and controls align with Microsoft's guidance on permission review and consent management (MS-REVIEW-1, MS-REVIEW-2). No invented capabilities, pricing, retention, or undocumented approval processes are asserted. All unknowns are explicitly identified, and no unsupported console paths or roles are assumed. The assessment correctly distinguishes delegated permissions from application permissions and clarifies that administrator consent does not confer an administrator role to ChatGPT.
